name: Noel Aubin
life: “I still remember sewing a coat around a seated client's favorite chair.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Noel by a small Sunday habit. Noel knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I measured seated and standing because dignity shouldn't disappear when she leans forward.
appearance: Noel has two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Look for a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a mustard canvas overshirt with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. In conversation Noel looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Noel has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To make the wearer comfortable seated and standing.
family: Rosa Marr is Noel’s cousin raised in the same household. Noel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Rosa remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The wrong bicycle*, Rosa says, “I found the missing bell screw in my dustpan.”
connections: Oakley Han (housecoat client). They measure a garment for a whole Sunday, including sitting at the head of the table.
